findings.description: Snapshot provenance attribute vocabulary is undefined, and the sealed proof binary requires an attribute snapshot records cannot honestly emit. crates/testkit/src/bin/proof/collection.rs hard-requires unisphere.source.offset on every validated record, while lane-contracts.json instructs snapshot lanes not to fake it; and no replacement names exist anywhere in the repository, so tk-0005 (snapshot half), tk-0006 and tk-0007 (IDE half) will each invent their own attribute keys and hard-code them into per-dialect fixtures. The resolution lives in crates/testkit/**, which no coder may touch. This is the specific counterexample to ac-0009's claim that all six owners can implement against frozen types without sibling dependencies: it holds for the five JSONL lanes and does not yet hold for the snapshot lanes, while ac-0008 makes provenance an acceptance requirement. Fix before dispatching those lanes: name the exact keys snapshot-derived records carry, state whether unisphere.source.offset is absent for them, and assign the proof's conditional required set to tk-0009.

findings.description: The tk-0007 unit interface contradicts itself and lane-contracts.json on names the PM alone must import at composition. The guide says CursorAdapterSnapshot while lane-contracts.json and the guide's own repeated boilerplate say CursorIdeAdapter; the same unit says 'DESCRIPTOR with id cursor' and then that DESCRIPTOR.id is cursor-transcript. A descriptor id is not internal - the Plan009 integration test asserts exact ids on the adapters list --json wire and its provenance test asserts the same string in emitted telemetry, so a wrong id is a published wire value. tk-0005's guide interface separately omits SNAPSHOT_DESCRIPTOR/copilot-cli-snapshot, which appears only in lane-contracts.json, so a coder reading only their unit packet ships one descriptor. Fix: state each exported const name and exact id in the unit interfaces, delete the superseded 'id cursor' clause, settle the type name in both files, and remove the Cursor boilerplate sentence from the five units where it is irrelevant - that duplication is how the contradiction propagated.

findings.description: Plan009's production provenance invariant has no named owner for snapshot registrations, so it can degrade silently while still passing. That test iterates the production ADAPTERS constant and invokes each entry's runner to assert emitted unisphere.source.adapter equals registration.descriptor.id; its whole value was that coverage extends automatically to the next registration. SnapshotAdapter has no runner and AdapterRegistration is {descriptor, run}, so at composition either snapshot descriptors join ADAPTERS with runners the test will invoke without a source, or they are registered elsewhere and three new identities silently drop out of D1's coverage. Neither the guide's tk-0009 interface nor lane-contracts.json says which, and no declared check names the invariant. Not blocking for any coder; blocking for the seal retaining the value it had last plan. Decide it in the tk-0009 interface before composition.

findings.description: No party is contractually required to call NativeSnapshot::validate. SnapshotLoader::read_snapshot takes SnapshotLimits and returns a NativeSnapshot, but neither the trait doc nor lane-contracts.json says the returned snapshot must satisfy validate(limits), and no mapper is told it may assume that; validate is also inherently post-hoc, measuring an already-materialized snapshot, so it cannot itself be the allocation guard. tk-0008's lane text does instruct enforcement before unbounded allocation, which is right, leaving validate a method with no named caller. Secondary asymmetry to settle at the same time: max_snapshot_bytes counts key.len() + bytes.len() while max_record_bytes bounds only bytes, so a single arbitrarily long native key - source-controlled in the SQLite case - is caught only in aggregate. Fix: state in lane-contracts.json that read_snapshot returns only snapshots for which validate(limits) is Ok, that limits are enforced during read, and that mappers may assume a validated snapshot.
findings.evidence: crates/core/src/snapshot.rs at 418a6245: 'pub trait SnapshotLoader { fn read_snapshot(&self, source: &SnapshotRef, limits: SnapshotLimits) -> Result<NativeSnapshot, PipelineError>; }' with no validate obligation; NativeSnapshot::validate accumulates record.key.len() + record.bytes.len() against max_snapshot_bytes while the RecordLimit check tests only record.bytes.len() > limits.max_record_bytes.
